# Scheduling benchmark (generated by scripts/run_benchmark.py)

Simulated schedules on Observed topology and labor data. 306 instances = 46 circuits × 3 damage sets (1 Observed Feb-2025 set + 2 seeded Poisson draws at 1×) × that circuit's distinct crew counts from {1, calibrated default, 2× default}: 36 circuits have two, 10 circuits have three (36 circuits' calibrated default is one crew, so for them 1 and the default coincide), i.e. 36 circuits × 3 sets × 2 crew counts + 10 circuits × 3 sets × 3 crew counts = 306. Every policy sees identical tasks, hours and crews. Metric: customer-outage hours (Σ customers × hours until service, each premise counted once; service returns only when every damaged zone on the path is repaired). 'Reduction' is 1 − ours/baseline; negative = we lost. Swap pass budget 0.5 s per instance. The headline figures are also written to benchmark_headline.json beside this file.

Rows overlap: the calibrated default is one crew for 36 of 46 circuits (Assumed: the crew count that clears the Observed Feb-2025 set in about 72 h of FIFO makespan, bounded to [1, 30]), so their default instances are also their 1-crew instances. The 'every circuit' row is the gain at each circuit's own default; the next row is the subset whose default exceeds one crew.

### Solver status

- Swap-improvement pass: ran on 306 instances, mean gain 1.39% (max 20.42%), runtime per dependency-aware solve mean 0.06 s, max 0.50 s (Measured).
- Exact reference (≤ 7 tasks, brute force over all orders): 64 instances; mean gap 0.19%, max gap 9.15%, instances at the optimum 60.
- With several crews the ordering is list-scheduled and therefore a heuristic; optimality holds only for one crew.

### Scale sanity check (not a fit)

At every circuit's own calibrated default crew count (46 Observed Feb-2025 damage sets, 36 of them at one crew), the dependency-aware schedule restores the last customer after a median of 1.5 days (10th–90th percentile 0.5–2.8 days). On the 10 circuits whose default exceeds one crew the median is 2.7 days (1.8–3.0). Observed: the organizer's day-granularity repair records for that storm show report→repair gaps of 0–6 days for 99.6% of records (median 1 day, 90th percentile 4 days, max 80 days; computed on 478 repaired reference-storm records (2025-02-12 to 2025-02-18) in the loaded bundle (demo bundle: 9 circuits); day-granularity dates). The crew default was calibrated to a 72 h FIFO makespan, so this agreement is partly by construction; it is a scale check, not validation.
